パパゲーノは「死ななかった脇役」から、a name for another route になった

Why did Papageno, a comic bird-catcher in Mozart’s The Magic Flute, become the name of a suicide-prevention media effect more than two centuries later? This essay moves from the 1791 opera to the Werther effect, the 2010 Papageno-effect study, later randomized trials and WHO guidance. The point is not simply to tell positive stories. Media also distributes models of what a person can do next when a crisis makes the future look closed.
